svg.aria-label: Diagram: Private Service Connect consumer endpoints in Google Cloud, the first mechanism in this block that gives you an address inside your own network; an endpoint is an internal IP address in the consumer VPC network that clients in that network reach directly, deployed as a forwarding rule referencing either a producer's service attachment, a bundle of global Google APIs, or a regional or multi-regional API; endpoints provide layer 4 connectivity only, so custom URLs and advanced traffic management require backends instead, which use network endpoint groups and put your own load balancer in front; interfaces are the third type and let the producer initiate connections back towards the consumer; for Google APIs this is presented as an alternative to Private Google Access, and unlike Private Google Access it can target regional and multi-regional APIs, lets you create several internal addresses for different uses, direct on-premises traffic at specific addresses and regions, and centralise API traffic through a load balancer for your own certificates and policies; the two API bundles all-apis and vpc-sc mirror the private and restricted VIP choice from the previous post; endpoints get automatic DNS names under p.googleapis.com derived from the endpoint name; and two sharp edges, that an existing Cloud DNS private zone for p.googleapis.com must be deleted before creating an endpoint or creation fails, and that an endpoint for Google APIs cannot be updated after it is created
svg.title: Private Service Connect consumer endpoints: an internal address of your own, at layer 4
svg.text: Four posts of reaching OUT to public addresses. This one brings the service IN.
An endpoint is an internal IP address in YOUR VPC network that your clients reach directly.
The definition that changes the shape of the problem
“Private Service Connect endpoints are INTERNAL IP ADDRESSES IN A CONSUMER VPC NETWORK
that can be directly accessed by clients in that network.”
No VIP, no public destination, no route to the internet gateway. Deployed as a FORWARDING RULE
referencing a service attachment, a bundle of global Google APIs, or a regional/multi-regional API.
ENDPOINTS
• Forwarding rule
• LAYER 4 only
• One internal IP mapped
to the service
• Consumer → producer
The simple case.
BACKENDS
• Network endpoint groups
• YOUR load balancer sits
in front
• Custom URLs, advanced
traffic management
When layer 4 isn’t enough.
INTERFACES
• The PRODUCER initiates
• Bidirectional
• Can live in the same VPC
network as the other two
• Producer → consumer
The other direction.
For Google APIs it is an ALTERNATIVE to Private Google Access — and it does more
• Endpoints can target a REGIONAL or MULTI-REGIONAL Google API — the rep.googleapis.com
endpoints that #90 and #92 both ruled out entirely.
• Create SEVERAL internal addresses for different use cases
• Direct on-premises traffic at specific addresses AND regions
• Centralise API traffic through a load balancer for your own certificates, policies, observability
“In this case, the producer is Google.”
The same choice as #92, in a different place
API_BUNDLE = all-apis → access to all supported APIs
API_BUNDLE = vpc-sc → restricted to APIs that support VPC Service Controls
Yesterday that decision was a DNS record. Here it is a flag on the endpoint.
What a service attachment carries, when the producer is not Google
• A CONSUMER ACCEPT LIST defining who may connect — the producer decides, not you
• A NAT SUBNET in the producer VPC, where translated traffic is sourced from
• An OPTIONAL DNS DOMAIN, used for entries created automatically in your Cloud DNS zone
Two sharp edges before you create one
1. If a Cloud DNS private zone for p.googleapis.com already exists, DELETE IT FIRST — otherwise
creation of the Service Directory DNS zone FAILS. Likely left behind by a previous attempt.
2. YOU CAN’T UPDATE an endpoint for Google APIs after it is created. Delete and recreate.
And each forwarding rule counts toward the per-VPC-network Private Service Connect quota.
DNS you get free: an endpoint named xyz yields storage-xyz.p.googleapis.com, compute-xyz.p.googleapis.com,
and the other commonly used APIs in the bundle — no zone to build by hand.
Endpoints also let two independent companies talk over internal IP addresses. That is the real unlock.
